title: Agents in Production: How OpenGov Built and Scaled OG Assist - Gabe De Mesa, OpenGov

takeaways.what_they_do: They run automated evals in CI against real model completions, checking whether the agent hit expected tools and did the intended action.
takeaways.evidence_quote: evals that run against real completions

takeaways.what_they_do: The agent loop pauses deterministically when a tool call requires approval, and a human explicitly accepts or rejects the mutating action.
takeaways.evidence_quote: deterministically interrupt the agent loop if there is a tool call approval required

takeaways.technique: Ephemeral sandboxes for code and files
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents execute code and create files in on-demand isolated sandboxes that are torn down afterward, keeping production systems out of reach.
takeaways.evidence_quote: whenever an agent tries to execute code or tries to create files, it does so in a sandbox

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep a running summary after N messages and retain only the most recent messages, with recall over the summary for older context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: give like a running summary after n number of messages

takeaways.what_they_do: They instrument the agent loop so function/tool calls produce spans and traces that can be profiled and cross-referenced across services.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you could profile all your traces
